source.title: Norm-Hierarchy Transitions in Representation Learning: When and Why Neural Networks Abandon Shortcuts
source.authors: Xuan Khanh Truong; Truong Quynh Hoa

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own weight-decay and norm-dynamics experiments on visual shortcut-learning tasks, extending delayed-transition claims to non-algorithmic settings. It does not reproduce the original modular-arithmetic grokking experiments in sufficient detail.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions modular-arithmetic results (including R2 > 0.97 and 293 runs), but says the full empirical details are deferred to concurrent work; these are not extracted as results here. The LLM emergent-abilities discussion is a hypothesis with predictions for future testing, not an experiment. The reported CIFAR, architecture, Waterbirds, and CelebA outcomes are included where they bear on delayed transitions or the weight-decay account.
record.test_reason: Only a thin test. The vision experiments (colored CIFAR-10, Waterbirds, CelebA) report final accuracy and weight-norm trajectories under weight-decay sweeps. The one result that bears on a version is CelebA: worst-group accuracy over epochs shows no sharp delayed jump at any λ. Waterbirds adds that no λ produces generalization to the worst group. Clean-accuracy timing is never reported for CIFAR-10, so norm peak-then-decay stands in for the delay, which is a related but different construct. The modular-arithmetic results are asserted (R2 > 0.97, 293 runs) but their data is deferred to other work.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors argue that delayed shortcut-to-structure transitions, grokking included, come from slow weight-decay-driven norm contraction. Predictive success depends on clean norm separation, and the 1/λ delay scaling fails on CIFAR-10. They also claim modular-arithmetic validation (6/6 predictions, R2 > 0.97) but defer its data. The LLM emergence link is explicitly a conjecture.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments focus on visual shortcut datasets and weight-decay/norm dynamics rather than reproducing the original small algorithmic-dataset grokking procedure or mechanistic Fourier-circuit analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with weight decay, shortcut correlation, architecture and normalisation, and dataset. In particular, GroupNorm has norm decay without corresponding clean-accuracy improvement; Waterbirds and CelebA are reported to lack clean norm separation.

fits_no_version.finding: On colored CIFAR-10, the weight-norm trajectory shifts with λ: it grows at weak λ, peaks then decays at intermediate λ, and is suppressed at strong λ. This holds across CNN and ResNet18 variants, and the output layer contracts more than the input layer. Clean-accuracy timing is never reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under weight decay, shortcut-learning image models show norm peak-then-decay dynamics that may signal a delayed shortcut-to-feature transition.

fits_no_version.finding: Final clean accuracy versus weight decay is an inverted U for ResNet18 (60.0/69.8/49.5% without normalization; 73.9/78.1/74.7% with BatchNorm). For SimpleCNN, weak λ scores as high as or higher than intermediate λ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intermediate weight decay maximizes final out-of-shortcut accuracy in spurious-feature vision tasks.

record.problems: The modular-arithmetic experiment is not described in full, despite summary claims; the paper says full empirical details are deferred. For the visual experiments, several results are reported as regime ranges or aggregate values, and clean-accuracy timing is generally not reported, limiting direct verification of delayed accuracy jumps. The quantitative delay law is explicitly reported not to hold on CIFAR-10.
record.rows_left_out: No reported modular-arithmetic result rows were extracted because the text defers its empirical details and provides no concrete condition-level measurements. The CelebA average-accuracy values and some additional norm-ordering results were not included because the selected rows capture the reported worst-group outcomes relevant to delayed generalization.

untested.parts: All of it. Modular-arithmetic results are only asserted, with no accuracy curves and no delay-versus-training-set-size data.
All of it. No circuit is identified; norm diagnostics are proposed but not related to a measured accuracy jump.
Accuracy timing on CIFAR-10. Initialization-scale manipulation. The lazy-to-rich transition, which is only discussed. Text and molecule data.
All of it. The LLM link is a stated conjecture.
All of it. There is no memorization-versus-circuit efficiency comparison, no dataset-size variation, no critical dataset size and no ungrokking.
All of it. AdamW is used throughout and no optimizer or numerical control is run.

missing.what: CelebA worst-group accuracy trajectory: stable above 86% after epoch 20, no sharp jump at intermediate λ. This is the only accuracy-timing evidence in the paper.

record.verdict_notes: The vision evidence rests on norm proxies. 'Delayed transition' is inferred from norm peak-then-decay, never from clean-accuracy curves. There are internal inconsistencies: the Figure 1 caption says accuracy peaks at intermediate λ, but the reported ranges show weak λ higher. Remark 2.5 writes Vsc < Vst, contradicting Definition 2.2. Seed counts differ between Figure 2 (3) and Section 5.4 (4). Table 3 gives CelebA 4/6 while CelebA itself shows no delay, and the Waterbirds count is given as both 1/4 and 2/6. The paper is a preprint. Both reproducibility and grokking claims depend on a concurrent paper that is not provided.

versions.untested_parts: No reported measurements of algorithmic-task training and test accuracy over time, delay versus training-set size, or the specified small-dataset grokking pattern.
No gradual formation or removal of a Fourier or other generalizing circuit is measured; no circuit progress measure is related to an accuracy jump.

Tests visual shortcut-learning settings and weight-decay regimes, but not initialization-scale interventions, an explicit lazy-to-rich transition, or delayed accuracy jumps tracked over time. No text or molecule experiment is reported.
LLM pretraining and fine-tuning are discussed only as a conjecture; no large-model training experiment is reported.

Weight decay, norms, and visual-task outcomes are studied, but the experiments do not test a critical dataset size or ungrokking below that size; no direct efficiency comparison of memorizing and generalizing circuits is reported.
No comparison establishes whether independent runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
No adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point softmax artifact is isolated or controlled as an explanation of delay.

rows.subject: SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Train with a weight-decay sweep on colored CIFAR-10; report clean accuracy and norm behavior by λ regime.
rows.measure: Final clean accuracy and total norm trajectory
rows.value: Clean accuracy 58–69%; norm grows to 5,000–14,000 with <1% decay.
rows.note: The reported norm behavior indicates persistent shortcut reliance, but no time series of clean accuracy is given to establish a delayed accuracy jump.
rows.check: Gives final clean accuracy and norm only; no accuracy-over-time, so a delayed jump cannot be read. Link to V5 removed: this measures shortcut versus real features, not memorization versus an efficient generalizing circuit, and dataset size is not varied. Also, weak λ reaches 58–69% clean accuracy, higher than intermediate λ (55–58%), which contradicts the caption's claim that accuracy peaks in the intermediate regime.

rows.subject: SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Train with a weight-decay sweep on colored CIFAR-10; report clean accuracy and norm behavior by λ regime.
rows.measure: Final clean accuracy and total norm trajectory
rows.value: Clean accuracy 55–58%; norm peaks then decays, by up to 21.6% at λ = 0.3.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars ±1 std over 4 seeds are stated for Figure 1; per-condition values not stated.
rows.note: The authors interpret peak-then-decay with clean accuracy as a delayed transition, but do not report clean-accuracy timing. The paper also says the quantitative T ∝ 1/λ prediction does not hold (r = −0.43).
rows.check: The norm peak-then-decay is a proxy, not a delayed rise in test accuracy. No clean-accuracy timing is given. V5 link removed for the same reason as r1.

rows.subject: SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Measure clean accuracy across four seeds at fixed weight decay and shortcut correlation.
rows.measure: Mean clean accuracy and norm trajectory reproducibility
rows.value: Mean clean accuracy 58.5% ± 2.3%; all runs show norm peak-then-decay.
rows.note: This is an aggregate across four seeds, as reported by the study; it does not establish an accuracy jump over time.
rows.check: Duplicates r6 (same 58.5% ± 2.3%). It is a reproducibility figure, not a delayed-generalization measure.

rows.subject: SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Measure total and per-layer norm dynamics during CIFAR-10 training.
rows.measure: Per-layer norm contraction from peak
rows.value: fc contracts 45%; conv1 contracts 31%; total norm grows 73%.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 4 states a shaded band of ±1 std over 4 seeds; exact errors not stated.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as output-to-input transition evidence. It measures layer norms, not the formation or removal of an identifiable generalizing circuit.
rows.check: Layer-norm contraction is a norm diagnostic, not a generalization measure. Total norm growing 73% also sits awkwardly with the claim of total-norm peak-then-decay elsewhere.

rows.subject: SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Train across weight decay values on Waterbirds and measure worst-group accuracy and norm dynamics.

conditions.value: Waterbirds; background correlated at 95% in training

rows.measure: Worst-group accuracy across λ and norm dynamics
rows.value: Worst-group accuracy is approximately 7.2–9.3% across λ, with no statistically significant ordering; at λ = 0.1, 8.2% ± 0.7%. Norm grows monotonically for λ ≤ 0.1; decay is 6.7% at λ = 0.3 and 56.3% at λ = 1.0.
rows.uncertainty: At λ = 0.1, ± 0.7% over three seeds; no uncertainty stated for the full range.
rows.note: The paper reports no worst-group improvement with intermediate regularisation and states that the norm-separation score is approximately 0.0.
rows.check: Worst-group accuracy stays around 7–9% at every λ, so weight decay switches on no transition within 100 epochs. The trajectory itself is not shown.

reader_labels.reason: The authors report norm peak-then-decay with clean-accuracy outcomes in the intermediate regime and across architecture variants, though accuracy timing is not directly reported (r2, r6, r8, r10–r16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Waterbirds worst-group accuracy does not improve across regularisation settings; CelebA shows no sharp accuracy jump, and the authors attribute both settings to absent clean norm separation (r18–r21).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Norm contraction and clean accuracy do not move uniformly together: strong regularisation suppresses norms and lowers CIFAR clean accuracy, and GroupNorm shows substantial norm decay without corresponding accuracy improvement; critical dataset size and ungrokking are not tested (r1–r3, r12, r14–r16).
